### `805d404` feat(count): count tokens with each model's encoding, exact via api
Claude, 2026-10-09

> Every count used cl100k_base, which is GPT-4's encoding: OpenAI models
> since GPT-4o use o200k_base, and Claude, Gemini and the other vendors
> use their own tokenizers, so the "Exact" label was only true for GPT-4.
>
> - --target-model picks the tiktoken encoding: o200k_base for GPT-4o,
>   GPT-4.1, GPT-5, GPT-6 and o-series models, cl100k_base otherwise.
> - Labels say when a count only approximates the model's tokenizer
>   (Claude, Gemini and other vendors, GPT-6 whose encoding is
>   unpublished, and the estimation fallback, which was labelled "Exact").
>   The @anthropic-ai/tokenizer package is the Claude 2 tokenizer and is
>   now labelled as an approximation.
> - New `ctxman count [path|-] --model ID [--api] [--json]`: counts a
>   project or piped text for a model and checks it against the window.
>   With --api it counts Claude models exactly through Anthropic's
>   count_tokens endpoint (free, nothing generated; needs the
>   @anthropic-ai/sdk package and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), batching files into
>   as few requests as possible and redacting secrets before sending.
> - tiktoken moves to dependencies so a plain `npm install ctxman` counts
>   exactly instead of estimating.
>

# Why: `isValidGitRef` in `lib/integrations/git/GitClient.js`

Context for explaining why this code looks the way it does, collected by `ctxman why` from the local git history and the repository (no network).

## Target

- File: `lib/integrations/git/GitClient.js`
- Symbol: `isValidGitRef` (function, declared on line 26)
- Lines: 19-28 of 354
- Revision: working tree (HEAD fda35dbdc7dc)

```javascript
/**
 * Check that a user-supplied revision (branch, tag, commit, HEAD~2, a..b) is safe to
 * hand to git: allowlisted characters only, and no leading '-' that git would parse
 * as an option (e.g. --output=<file>)
 * @param {string} ref
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export function isValidGitRef(ref) {
  return typeof ref === 'string' && !ref.startsWith('-') && /^[a-zA-Z0-9/\-_.@^~]+$/.test(ref);
}
```

## History

1 commit that changed lines 19-28 (`git log -L`), newest first.

### 1. fix(git): run git without a shell and validate user-supplied refs

`6939d13` · 2026-10-06 · Claude

> GitClient.exec() built a command line and ran it through execSync, so
> any git ref was parsed by /bin/sh. Its only guard rejected ';' and '&'.
> Refs reach it from untrusted input:
> - REST GET /api/v1/diff?since=. The server binds to localhost, has no
>   auth token by default and sends CORS *, so a web page can issue the
>   request.
> - The MCP git_diff tool's `branch` argument, which a model controls.
> - `--changed-since`.
> `ctxman github` also interpolated the URL's owner/repo/branch into a
> `git clone` command line.
>
> - GitClient.exec() now takes an argument array and uses
>   execFileSync('git', args): no shell, arguments reach git verbatim.
>   File paths go after `--`.
> - New isValidGitRef()/assertGitRef(). They allowlist ref characters
>   and reject a leading '-', so a ref cannot become a git option such as
>   --output. getChangedFiles, DiffAnalyzer.getFileDiff,
>   compareBranches and getRangeStats validate before running git.
> - REST answers 400 for an invalid `since`. MCP git_diff returns
>   isError for an invalid ref or a git failure instead of plain text.
> - GitUtils.cloneRepository validates the branch and runs
>   `git clone ... -- <url> <dir>` via execFileSync.
>
> The new test/git-ref-injection.test.js uses a real temp repository. It
> feeds hostile refs (shell substitution, pipes, newlines, option
> injection) to GitClient, DiffAnalyzer and the REST endpoint, and
> checks that nothing runs and normal refs still work. Four of its five
> cases fail before this change. Existing unit tests are updated for the
> argv call shape.
>
> Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
